script.base: Cincinnati is a 5.5-point home favorite with a 24.5 implied total and should lead by about a score in a moderate-pace game (43.5 is neither a shootout nor a slog). Chase (45 targets, 365 yards, 433 air yards in weeks 5-7) and Higgins (25 targets, 180 yards, 302 air) carry the pass game against a Jets secondary missing Sauce Gardner; Chase Brown (28 carries, 177 yards L3) runs the clock late. The Jets (implied 19.0) trail without Garrett Wilson and Josh Reynolds, so Justin Fields (17 carries, 80 rush yards L3) scrambles and the leftover targets (Mason Taylor if active, Isaiah Davis, Tyler Johnson, Lazard, Ruckert) absorb a pass-heavier dog script.
script.flip1: Cincinnati gets up big early, Brown's carries pile up, and late WR snaps stall the way a clock-killing favorite caps QB/WR yards. Chase's 94.5 is the first leg to die; Higgins at 33.5 can still be home if the explosives come before the stall. A trailing Jets offense abandons the run, which would also bury a Breece Hall rush over if he plays on the bad knee.
script.flip2: It stays a one-score game. Fields plus Cincinnati's leaky run defense (4.83 YPC, 22 runs of 10+) keep New York on schedule, Hall (Questionable) gets a full carry share if the knee holds, and both passing games stay live so Chase and Higgins clear more easily. A Hendrickson sit (Questionable, hip) on top of Sample Doubtful and Cedric Johnson Out would further help Fields sustain drives and push this flip.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and the Higgins over lost, with Chase under 94.5 alongside it. Matt Lee was inactive, interior pressure arrived, and Cincinnati still covered by handing Brown the ball in a clock-kill — the 27- and 42-yard Brown games show that script, and the 108-yard game shows the ceiling. Chase had a full target day and landed on 94 or in the 70s, a fine stat line that loses 94.5, which was already the market's Sauce number. Higgins repeated the 22-yard outing because Chase took 15 targets again in a 43.5-total game and the backup corner was not the pushover the right-side YPA suggested. The same Monday, a Hall rush under would also have been the wrong drop-check if he played and ripped the 4.83 YPC Bengals front on one explosive, or the ticket would have been a void if the knee scratched him — which is why that lean was not kept. Weather was never in the file, so a windy outdoor afternoon that killed deep balls is an uncheckable extra way both overs lose.
slip_story: One story: Cincinnati's passing game against a Gardner-less Jets secondary in a one-score home favorite script, not a shootout stack and not a clock-kill RB stack. Higgins over 33.5 is the number; Chase over 94.5 is the correlated primary-target anchor and is script-dependent on the game not becoming a run-out. They win together if Cincinnati throws. They lose together if Lee's absence plus a Brown clock-kill compresses air yards. Do not add a total under, a Hall rush over, or a Jets WR over to this slip — those need the other flip. Two legs, one market per player, no TDs. Allen is not added unless Hall is later ruled out.
